request: Run bring-down on this: assess two candidates in our Node.js 22 TypeScript API, one repository owned by one team of four. First: `src/lib/retry.ts` is 140 lines of hand-written retry with exponential backoff around outbound HTTP calls. It took six bug-fix commits last quarter, two of them after production incidents in which it retried non-idempotent POST requests. Every outbound call already goes through `got` 14, which is in `package.json` and on our platform team's approved list; `got` has a built-in `retry` option that we switch off, and nothing in our wrapper is specific to our domain. Second: three modules in this repository each carry a copy of a 40-line `isEligibleForDiscount` function that encodes our own discount policy. The copies are identical, and a teammate proposes moving them into `src/shared/discount.ts`, which this same team would maintain. What should move down, and where does each one land?

expect.criterion: bring-down #1: a question about replacing custom code with a lower-level capability loads the bring-down method
bring-down #2: commodity code covered by an approved library moves from L4 CODE to L3 LIB, named by level and acronym
bring-down #3: a move names the exact capability it lands in
bring-down #4: a move names the current and the target maintenance owner
bring-down #5: a move that keeps the same maintenance owner is excluded with its reason
bring-down #6: an extraction inside the same repository is handed to the architecture skills
summary-led-report #2: the decision opens with the four blocks in order
